method: Individual reading of PDF pages 21–23; reported personal experiences remain attributed, and nonstandard source wording is not repaired without audio.
words: local branches of an organization that are currently operating
全国各地仍在运作的分会
Active means operating, not simply energetic; chapters are local branches. Picture a map with the currently operating branches lit up.
The organization has active chapters in several cities.
该组织在多个城市设有仍在运作的分会。
The approximate count is a recorded claim, not a live organizational total.
having the eyes covered so that one cannot see
blindfold + -ed adds /ɪd/ after /d/. Connect the noun blindfold, the cloth, with the state blindfolded.
The participant was blindfolded during the game.
游戏过程中，这名参与者被蒙住了眼睛。
Passive state in an attributed account; no staging of the harmful initiation in the teaching example.
not having enough of something necessary or desirable
deprive drops final e before -ed: deprived. Remember deprived of something, and the compound sleep-deprived.
After the long journey, we felt sleep-deprived.
长途旅行之后，我们觉得睡眠不足。
Sleep deprivation in the source, not necessarily economic deprivation.
to continue through something difficult or painful
Connect endure with endurance: the ability to keep going through difficulty. Stress the second syllable.
They had to endure a long delay.
他们不得不忍受长时间的延误。
Conditional ability to get through the next hours, not approval that participants should accept harm.
a student in the first year of high school or university in the US
Fresh suggests new; freshman is a new first-year student. Plural freshmen changes man to men, while freshman year keeps the singular modifier.
She joined the club during her freshman year.
她在大一时加入了这个社团。
First university year in this account, not a gender restriction on the student's identity.
a process or ceremony through which someone joins a group
initiate drops final e and adds -ion: initiation. Connect initial, the beginning, with the start of membership.
The club held a short initiation ceremony.
俱乐部举行了一场简短的入会仪式。
Initiation does not inherently mean hazing; the specific harmful conduct is alleged separately.
physical + -ly specifies the body; exhausted means used up, like an exhausted supply. Picture bodily energy depleted.
After the move, I felt physically exhausted.
搬家之后，我感到身体筋疲力尽。
Bodily fatigue in the attributed account, distinct from emotional exhaustion.
committed to joining a fraternity or having gone through its pledge process
已承诺入会的；经历入会过程的
pledge adds only d because it ends in e: pledged. Keep the /dʒd/ ending; don't add a separate vowel.
He pledged a fraternity in his first year.
他大一时报名加入了一个兄弟会。
Source says fully fledged, fully pledged as wordplay/self-repair. Fully fledged means fully established; fully pledged is not a universal formal membership category.
the edge of a steep drop; figuratively, a point just before a major change
悬崖边缘；重大变化的边缘
Picture a person at a cliff edge to remember precipice. On the precipice of + -ing suggests being very close to a consequential change.
The company was on the precipice of a major change.
公司正处于重大变化的关口。
Source metaphor refers to impending membership and continues into 340; no literal cliff.
relating to the mind, feelings, or mental processes
psychology becomes psychological. Initial ps sounds /s/; connect the word with mental experience rather than physical injury.
The report discussed the psychological effects of the event.
报告讨论了这一事件的心理影响。
Reported mental harm, not a diagnosis established by this review.
connected to and useful for understanding the matter being discussed
Learn relevant to + topic, not relevant with. Imagine sorting information into connected and unrelated piles.
Please include only information relevant to the question.
请只加入与这个问题相关的信息。
Earlier separate experience is said to be relevant, not part of the same alleged event.
to express an idea or feeling clearly in words
The verb articulate ends in /leɪt/; the adjective articulate has a reduced ending. Here unable to requires the verb: put feelings into words.
She found it difficult to articulate her concerns.
她发现很难清楚表达自己的担忧。
Verb for expression, not the adjective describing an eloquent person.
feeling distress or embarrassment about oneself or something one has done or experienced
Shame is the feeling; ashamed describes the person feeling it. Use ashamed of + noun/-ing, not ashamed for everything.
He felt ashamed of hiding the mistake.
他为隐瞒这个错误感到羞愧。
The speaker reports shame about vulnerability; this does not imply he was responsible for harm done to him.
a pungent red pepper used as a spice, usually in powdered form
Remember the two beats kai-EN, stressing the second. Anchor the unusual spelling cayenne to the spice label cayenne pepper.
The recipe calls for a pinch of cayenne pepper.
食谱要求加入少许卡宴辣椒粉。
Ingredient named in the account; teaching example uses ordinary food preparation, not harmful application.
a box in which a dead person is placed for burial
Remember double f in coffin by picturing the two long sides of a box. It is a burial box, not coffee.
The museum displayed an old wooden coffin.
博物馆展出了一口古老的木棺。
Object in an attributed initiation account; the account does not describe the person as dead.
formally admitted into an organization or role
被正式接纳入会；被引入某职务
induct ends in /t/, so inducted adds /ɪd/. Link induction with the formal moment of joining, followed by into.
The new members were inducted into the club.
新成员被正式接纳加入俱乐部。
Formal admission, not the unrelated scientific induction sense.
causing someone to suffer harm, pain, or an unwanted burden
Learn inflict harm on someone as a complete pattern. The harm is the object; on introduces the affected person.
The report accused the group of inflicting emotional harm.
报告指责该团体造成了心理伤害。
The account explicitly says he did not consent; attribution remains intact.
a small door in a floor or ceiling giving access to another space
地板或天花板上的活板门
Trap door names a hidden or horizontal access door. Picture a panel opening in a floor, not a door meant to catch an animal.
A trap door led to the storage space below.
一扇活板门通向下面的储物空间。
Physical access opening, not a metaphorical trap.
a sour liquid used in cooking or preserving food
Say vinegar in three beats, VIN-uh-ger, with the stress first. Anchor it to the sour taste of a bottle of vinegar.
Add a little vinegar to the dressing.
Ingredient vocabulary; everyday food example avoids reenacting the alleged abuse.
the state of being exposed to harm or emotional hurt
vulnerable changes -able to -ability: vulnerability. Connect being vulnerable with needing care, not being at fault.
She spoke openly about her sense of vulnerability.
她坦率地谈到了自己的脆弱感。
Personal feeling in the quoted account; no blame is assigned for being vulnerable.
the band of fabric around the waist of trousers, shorts, or a skirt
waist + band gives waistband: a band around the waist. Distinguish waist from waste by picturing clothing.
These shorts have an elastic waistband.
Clothing part in the quoted account; teaching example remains neutral.
a condition involving compulsive dependence on a substance or activity
Connect addicted with addiction: the adjective describes dependence and the noun names the condition. Stress -DIC-.
The article discussed support for people struggling with addiction.
文章讨论了如何支持受成瘾问题困扰的人。
The quoted criticism concerns glorifying dependence; no diagnosis of a named person.
the act of gaining control or a victory; here, a boastful way of treating sexual partners as achievements
征服；（此处）把性关系当作战绩
Connect conquest with conquer: both evoke winning control. Sexual conquest applies a victory metaphor to people and can be objectifying.
The essay criticized the language of sexual conquest.
这篇文章批评了把性关系描述为征服战绩的说法。
Critically quoted objectifying framing, not a term the lesson endorses as a positive social goal.
thrown away or left because no longer wanted
discard means throw away; after its final /d/, -ed is /ɪd/. Picture items set aside for disposal.
Discarded furniture filled the empty room.
空房间里堆满了废弃家具。
Unwanted objects shown in a video, not evidence establishing why they were left.
Glory names the praise; glorious describes something seen as splendid. In the source, the speaker criticizes what the group treats as glory.
The team valued cooperation more than personal glory.
团队重视合作，胜过个人荣耀。
Part of a critical framing contrast; not approval of sexual conquest.
things made available or offered to people
offer + -ing makes an offering, something offered; plural offerings can mean services or opportunities, not only religious gifts.
The center expanded its educational offerings.
这个中心增加了教育项目。
Access to substances and social opportunities in the account, not religious sacrifice.
not occupied or currently in use
Connect vacant with vacancy: an unoccupied room has a vacancy. Picture an empty room rather than an available holiday.
The building has been vacant for months.
这栋楼已经空置了几个月。
Occupancy at the video's/recording's time, not a live status check.
relating to the body rather than the mind
Physical begins with ph pronounced /f/. Contrast physical with psychological in the source's list of harms.
这份工作需要体力劳动。
Body-related harm, not the separate sense of a tangible object.
officially prevented from entering or taking part
bar doubles r before -ed: barred. Picture a bar across an entrance; use barred from + place or -ing.
Visitors were barred from entering the closed area.
访客被禁止进入封闭区域。
Reported campus exclusion of a chapter; does not itself mean a criminal conviction.
currently operating or participating rather than inactive
act + -ive describes involvement or operation. Here active contrasts with closed or inactive, not merely physically energetic.
The group remains active in the community.
这个团体仍在社区中开展活动。
Operating-status adjective in the chapter count; no current total certified.
a female student social organization at a US college or university
Sorority is the counterpart of fraternity in this campus context. Link it with sisterhood; stress -ROR-.
She joined a sorority during college.
她上大学时加入了一个姐妹会。
Organization pictured on a poster; membership in that photograph does not connect the people to the alleged incident.
a potent synthetic opioid used medically for severe pain and also found in illicit drug supplies
芬太尼，一种强效合成阿片类药物
Remember the three beats FEN-ta-nyl, stressing the first. This is a specific substance name, not a general word for all drugs.
The report mentioned a fentanyl test.
报告提到了一项芬太尼检测。
An object described in a video does not prove substance use, a test result or who used it. No testing/medical instructions supplied.
phrases: close to
almost or approximately a stated number
接近；将近
Close to fifty people attended.
将近五十人出席了。
Numerical approximation, not physical proximity.
screamed bloody murder
screamed extremely loudly, usually in distress or protest
大声惨叫；拼命尖叫
He screamed bloody murder when he saw the spider.
他看到蜘蛛时吓得大声尖叫。
Informal idiom; does not mean that a murder actually occurred. Source is an attributed report of distress.
wash off
remove something from a surface using washing
洗掉
Wash off the mud before you come inside.
进屋前先把泥洗掉。
Phrasal verb taught with a neutral example; original mention of milk is not presented as treatment advice.
frame addiction as valor
present addiction as though it were courage or something admirable
把成瘾包装成勇气
The article criticized attempts to frame addiction as valor.
文章批评了把成瘾包装成勇气的做法。
Reusable frame A as B means portray A as B; valor means courage. This is a critical description, not praise.
leftover food
food remaining after a meal or use
剩饭剩菜；剩余食物
Put the leftover food in a container.
把剩下的食物装进容器里。
Leftover modifies food; leftovers can stand alone as a plural noun.
segments: Turned 250 uses an age verb for the country; age is relative to recording, not a request to alter original wording.
Active means operating local branches; about marks an approximate narrated count, not a live total.
It's said attributes the approximate count; living members includes alumni still alive, clarified in 329–331.
Introduces presence of a local branch at Cornell, continued with the founding date in 327.
Present perfect plus since marks duration from a starting year; Xi is the branch's name, not an ordinary English word.
Been around means existed for a long time, not traveled around physically.
Question checks whether the count means simultaneous students; the next answers explicitly correct this interpretation.
Living means alive, not living together in one house; clarification answers 329.
Explains that the living-member total includes people who are no longer students.
Introduces a separate older account; pledge is a prospective member, not a monetary promise.
Explicitly separates the historical account from the Jane Doe case while asserting a connection in topic.
Recounts means tells a past experience; this remains a useful reporting-verb gap rather than automatic coverage from hazing.
He's like introduces reported speech informally; not a statement about similarity.
Locates the earlier membership at the same institution; does not merge the two time periods or allegations.
He says attributes the list of harms; physical and psychological are distinguished, and freshman is first-year student.
Self-repair on the this is is retained in source; completed thought identifies the initiation night.
Metaphorical brink, not a cliff; a is completed by member in 340. Do not turn the fragment into an invented standalone sentence.
Fully fledged versus fully pledged is a spoken correction/play on words; the fixed fully fledged adjective needs explicit teaching beyond pledged alone.
Tossed onto a sheet and flinging up and down remain physical-action barriers; the account is introduced as an allegation.
Tossing him up illustrates prior physical action, but gesture-dependent like this cannot be reconstructed from the PDF.
Essayed is euphemistic/ASR wording in the source, not essay writing; do not silently normalize the quoted allegation without audio.
Short temporal description continuing the attributed account; no additional lexical barrier.
Slathered, fistfuls, genitals and the locally named mixture mung create barriers beyond waistband; keep explicit account attributed and avoid instructional examples.
First-person feeling statement within the quotation; no new idiom.
Rhetorical question introduces the explanation in 348; mung is a local label, not automatically mung beans.
Oatmeal and consisted of remain learner targets; source lists contents, but the lesson must not turn it into a recipe for abuse.
Consent to + -ing and smeared still need support; screamed bloody murder is an idiom for loud distress, not literal murder. Explicit absence of consent preserved.
Junk is slang for genitals here, not rubbish, and gallon is a volume measure. Reported response is not promoted as treatment advice.
Made to crawl is passive compulsion; crawl needs a clear physical-action definition. Source has no explicit new subject supplied by us.
Pressured to solve a riddle contrasts expected puzzle solution with the later discovery that none existed; as it turned out reports later information.
Collapsed is a physical-action/medical-state verb needing a contextual definition; do not infer cause or diagnosis from one sentence.
Passive sequence: placed, lowered, formally admitted. Coffin is a prop in the account, not evidence of death; chapter room belongs to the local group.
Infamous and inconsistent Kai-Fi versus Chi Phi spelling remain issues. Preserve printed proper name and avoid inventing an official spelling correction in the quotation.
Like the houses is unclear after made posters for parties; preserve possible disfluency/ASR error without inventing the intended clause.
Great Fratsby is a fraternity-themed pun on The Great Gatsby; needs a cultural reference note rather than treating it as a normal adjective+noun phrase.
Articulate means express verbally; process pain here means make sense of an emotional experience, distinct from the Unit 5 noun process. Shame is reported, not blame assigned by the lesson.

Offerings are things made available; accepted access to is the quoted speaker's retrospective account. But continues the contrast into 360; girls wording is not adopted as an endorsed way to describe people.
Social license means group permission/acceptance, not a legal license. Frame A as B critically describes presenting harmful behavior as admirable; valor explained in the phrase note.
Piece means an article, not a physical piece; Cornell Sun is the named publication. Published recently is relative to recording time.
Worth + -ing recommends the article; not worth to read or a monetary price.
Long relative clause identifies the house; now vacant means unoccupied at the described time, not that its history is erased.
Present perfect since gives a continuing closure state; reported year is preserved rather than reconciled against external case history.
Barred from campus means excluded; chapter is the branch, not the entire national organization, and chronology is attributed to the narrator.
Reaction checks causal connection with the previously mentioned case, not a new factual assertion.
Short confirmation of the narrated date; not independent verification of the closure.
Video description of a now-empty room; discarded furniture and leftover food name objects, not evidence establishing who left them.
Sorority is a female student organization; a poster depicting members does not implicate them in the case.
Self-repair all of their, it's like clarifies a group photograph; no additional people or ownership details invented.
A test object is named; this does not establish a result, substance use or ownership.
Rhetorical question expresses surprise at the object; no answer about actual drug use or test interpretation inferred.
Liquor bottles adds the spirits sense of liquor; alcohol alone does not teach the beer-versus-liquor distinction.
Reiterates present emptiness, in contrast with the past occupancy stated next.
Not empty contrasts with now; allegedly scopes the case occurrence and October 2024 is quoted chronology, not independently verified.
